tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (connection timeouts, refused connections, one-way traffic, slow transfers, etc.) rather than implementation details, and explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the problem directly ('even if they don't name the problem'). It also explicitly excludes an out-of-scope case (DNS resolution failures) with a pointer to another skill, which sharpens scope. It is a longish paragraph but remains within the 'short paragraph' allowance given the breadth of triggers it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user is troubleshooting AWS network connectivity: a connection times out, is refused, or resets; traffic flows only one way; flow logs show REJECT... Also use it whenever the user shares or describes VPC Flow Logs or a packet capture... even if they don't name the problem."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures (flow log formats, SG vs NACL inference, Wireshark flag analysis) without explaining generic concepts like what a packet or TCP is. It assumes the agent already knows networking basics and focuses on non-obvious AWS/Wireshark-specific facts.
tests.evidence: Request ACCEPT plus response REJECT on the same ENI points to a network ACL (NACLs are stateless; SGs are stateful).

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (field definitions, query syntax, playbooks) is consistently delegated to references/ files rather than embedded in the body; the body only states core rules and when to load each reference.
tests.evidence: Load references/vpc-flow-logs.md to interpret any flow log record. It holds the field definitions, flag values, address translation, and traffic that isn't logged.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body: flow-log-queries.md, preparing-evidence.md, vpc-flow-logs.md, wireshark-analysis.md, packet-capture-analysis.md, troubleshooting-playbooks.md.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition for when to load it, both inline in the workflow steps and in the final References list.
tests.evidence: [references/vpc-flow-logs.md](references/vpc-flow-logs.md): when interpreting any flow log record (fields v2 to v11, SG vs NACL inference, tcp-flags, address translation, unlogged traffic)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (classification of evidence, read-only confirmation commands, mutation restrictions) are prescriptive with exact rules, while interpretive sections (interpreting captures, root cause analysis) give reasoning-based guidance rather than rigid steps, appropriately matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: This skill is read-only. It never changes security groups, network ACLs, routes, flow logs, or mirroring sessions.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where tool choices arise (e.g., CloudWatch Logs Insights vs Athena, tshark vs tcpdump), the skill designates defaults or treats both as acceptable scoped options rather than presenting an unstructured menu of many choices.
tests.evidence: Query them in CloudWatch Logs or Athena, or read an export the user attaches.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (classify evidence path, collect scoped evidence, interpret with documented behavior, confirm, self-check) applicable to any network troubleshooting instance rather than a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: Decide which path applies before collecting anything: Path A: flow logs reachable in the account... Path B: the user has or must provide evidence.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes numerous concrete, non-obvious domain corrections functioning as gotchas throughout the Step 3 interpretation sections, even without a dedicated 'Gotchas' heading.
tests.evidence: tcp-flags are OR-ed per record, so match the bit, not one exact value... Some traffic is not logged, and SKIPDATA intervals hide flows, so a missing record isn't proof that traffic didn't happen.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill defines a detailed structured output format directly in the Output requirements section, satisfying the need for templates for reports/findings.
tests.evidence: Full form, when there's evidence or account data to analyze. Every response must include: 1. Assumptions... 2. Findings... 3. Coverage gaps...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The inline output template in 'Output requirements' is a numbered list of ~20 short bullet items, not an oversized skeleton; it stays within the acceptable inline length and isn't excessive reference material.
tests.evidence: 1. Assumptions: capture point, flow log format and fields, time window, filters applied. 2. Findings, most severe first...
